title: Thing page fixes: the hero runs up behind the masthead as one screen, the masthead and footer keep the site's gutters, the engine's header rule stops reaching the deck's exhibits
first: Map: gamecult-site docs/masthead-campaign.md, sections 'Body facts' B6-B8 and 'The shape' > '/Thing: the hero runs up behind the masthead'. Ruling thing:ruling:operator-deck-is-a-site-page stands (masthead kept, deck fills the screen). The operator's new words, verbatim in the map: 'any reason the masthead has its own background separate from the page background? I feel like it could easily take up that same space', the arrow pointing from the masthead down into the hero.

Soul findings this cut resolves: thing:finding:cut-deck-site-page.s1.engine-header-leak (Medium) and thing:finding:cut-deck-site-page.s1.chrome-edges (Low). thing:finding:cut-deck-site-page.s1.body-under-scrollbar is NOT in this cut: it is question scrollbar-fix-home (engine vs site-override); under site-override one rule html { width: auto } is added to custom.scss outside the Thing block, otherwise nothing here changes.

The frame (GameCult-Quartz renderPage.tsx 271-290): .page > #quartz-body is the grid; .center is one grid item holding .page-header, article, hr, .page-footer; the site footer is .center's sibling in grid-footer. The stacking below lives inside .center and needs no engine edit. The engine's Header.css sets header { display:flex; align-items:center; margin:2rem 0; gap:1.5rem } globally.

The deck stage (deck.css 479) is 100svh, position:relative without z-index, overflow:hidden, flex column centred; its children #burst (z 3) and .flash (z 4) would paint over a header with a lower z-index. deck.js already has a resize listener calling sizeCanvas and sizeBurst (last 6 lines of the file).

Gutters elsewhere: .page padding 0 1.2rem (custom.scss 32) plus #quartz-body padding 0 1rem below $desktop 1200px (base.scss) and .page padding 0 0.7rem at $mobile 800px (custom.scss 1432). The Thing block zeroes both, so the inset it gives back must equal their sum per breakpoint: 1.2rem desktop, 2.2rem tablet, 1.7rem mobile.
Deploy is push to main -> workflow 'Deploy Quartz' -> GitHub Pages at gamecult.org; small commits; CI is the verifier. A local .\scripts\quartz\quartz.ps1 build is optional on Starfire.

deletes.note: Inside body[data-slug="Thing"]: the .page-header rule (max-width 1680px; margin-inline auto; padding 0 1.2rem) is replaced by the stacked header rule in adds; the standalone padding value 1.2rem goes because the inset becomes var(--thing-inset).

keeps_moves: The deck's markup in GameCult/Thing.md, its exhibits, copy, numbers, HUD, ticker and every animation are unchanged. Soul diffs Thing.md against base and expects no change.
The masthead itself (GameCultMasthead.tsx, .gamecult-titlebar* rules, the card rule at custom.scss 646) is not touched by this cut; the card's removal is the site-masthead campaign's cut flat-nav.
The HUD pill's phone position (top-right, fixed) is kept; its overlap with the masthead's community icons until first scroll was accepted in the Thing map r4.
The stage stays 100svh tall and keeps its own ground var(--inv) #03070d, its .hero-bg and .rays; only its top padding changes.
adds: custom.scss, Thing block, the variable: body[data-slug="Thing"] { --thing-inset: 1.2rem; @media all and (max-width: 1200px) { --thing-inset: 2.2rem } @media all and (max-width: 800px) { --thing-inset: 1.7rem } } (use the engine's $desktop/$mobile tokens if custom.scss already imports variables.scss, as it does at line 2; otherwise the literal px values).

custom.scss, Thing block, the stack: .page > #quartz-body .center { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); grid-template-areas: "stack" "foot"; } .page > #quartz-body .center > .page-header { grid-area: stack; z-index: 5; align-self: start; justify-self: center; width: 100%; max-width: 1680px; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 0 var(--thing-inset); } .page > #quartz-body .center > article { grid-area: stack; min-width: 0; } .page > #quartz-body .center > .page-footer { grid-area: foot; }. The existing margin-top on .page-header (2.4rem desktop, 1.3rem mobile from the site-wide rules at 638 and 1435) still applies and is the masthead's distance from the top of the hero.

custom.scss, Thing block, the footer: .page > #quartz-body > footer { width: 100%; max-width: 1680px; margin-inline: auto; box-sizing: border-box; padding-inline: var(--thing-inset); } so the footer's links start where they do on /Projects at every width.

deck.css line 479, .thing-deck .stage: add padding-top: var(--masthead-h, 9rem). The stage is border-box and flex-centres .hero-in in the remaining height, so the hero content clears the masthead and masthead plus hero is one screen.

deck.css line 461, .thing-deck .xhead: add align-items: stretch; margin: 0 so the engine's header rule decides nothing inside an exhibit header. Reach-in guards (line 689): add .thing-deck h1 { font-size: inherit } to the h1,h2,h3 guard line or as its own line.

deck.js, beside sizeCanvas/sizeBurst: var hdr=document.querySelector('.page-header'); function sizeHead(){ if(hdr) root.style.setProperty('--masthead-h', hdr.offsetHeight+'px'); } called at init before frame() and inside the existing resize listener before sizeCanvas(). Also call it in the document.fonts.ready handler (line 147) since the masthead's height changes when Montserrat arrives.

file_changes.change: the Thing block: --thing-inset per breakpoint; .center as the two-row stack; .page-header stacked over article with z-index 5 and the inset; .page-footer in row foot; the site footer insetted; the old .page-header rule replaced.
sizeHead() defined and called at init, in the resize listener and in the fonts.ready handler.

authority_map.owner: custom.scss under body[data-slug="Thing"] owns the page chrome on the Thing page: the stacking of masthead over hero and the inset of masthead and footer. deck.css owns the hero's clearance (the stage's top padding) and the exhibit headers' layout. deck.js owns the measured masthead height as a display-only variable on the deck root. The engine owns the frame and its Header rule and is not edited.
inputs: the measured height of .page-header on the Thing page (deck.js)
the site's gutters per breakpoint (custom.scss 32 and 1432, base.scss #quartz-body padding), mirrored as --thing-inset
the deck's existing stage, hero and exhibit rules
outputs: https://gamecult.org/Thing: the first viewport is the masthead over the hero's ground and rays, the hero content below the masthead, one screen in all
the Thing page's masthead and footer inset equal to /Projects at 1440, 1000 and 375
derived_state: --masthead-h: display-only, derived from layout by deck.js on init, resize and font load; the CSS fallback 9rem is for a script-less load
--thing-inset: derived from the breakpoint; decides nothing on any other page
the one-column grid from empty sidebars, unchanged
forbidden_writers: no engine edit: renderPage.tsx, Header.tsx and base.scss are unchanged (the scrollbar fix is its own question and its own cut)
no site rule targets anything inside .thing-deck; the stage padding and xhead fix live in deck.css
no change to the deck's markup, copy, numbers or animations
no fixed or absolute positioning of the masthead; it scrolls away with the page as on every other page
no second inset value: the masthead and the footer both read --thing-inset
shared_paths: the same slug-block mechanism the Graph and the sleeping-colossus post use
the same Deploy Quartz workflow and Pages origin
the same resize path deck.js already uses for its canvases
authority_map.deletion_line: the Thing block's old .page-header rule (max-width, margin-inline, padding 0 1.2rem) is removed before the stacked header rule is written; no rule in the block carries a literal gutter after this cut.

builds: Deploy Quartz on GameCult/gamecult-site green for the landing commit: gh run list -R GameCult/gamecult-site -w "Deploy Quartz" -L 1

the .page-header rules inside body[data-slug="Thing"]: no match (the masthead is a grid item in flow).
site/quartz/static/thing/deck.css: no match on any rule line outside @keyframes bodies (every rule still starts with .thing-deck).
